blocks.name: Diagrammatic Analysis of the Labour Market

blocks.text: Diagrammatic Analysis of the Labour Market

blocks.md:
- **Labour market equilibrium** occurs when the **demand for labour (D**<sub>**L**</sub>**)** is equal to the **supply of labour (S**<sub>**L**</sub>**)**

  - The D<sub>L</sub> is the demand **by firms** for workers
  - The S<sub>L</sub> is the supply of labour **by workers**
- Individual firms are ***price takers*** in the labour market as they have to accept the **wage rate **that workers are being paid in the industry

  - If they offer a** lower wage,** they will likely struggle to recruit workers
  - If they offer a **higher wage,** there will be an excess supply of  workers applying to work there

blocks.caption: In the labour market for graphic designers, the equilibrium wage rate is W and the equilibrium quantity is Q. At this point the DL = SL

blocks.md:
- The market for graphic designers is in **equilibrium, where D**<sub>**L **</sub>**= S**<sub>**L**</sub>** **
- The **equilibrium wage** is W and the **quantity** of labour is Q
- There is **no *****excess supply*** of labour
- There is **no***** excess demand*** for labour

blocks.name: The Effect of a Rise in Demand for Labour

blocks.text: The Effect of a Rise in the Demand for Labour

blocks.md:
- A rise in the demand for labour will shift the demand curve for labour  to the right
- This causes an increase in the equilibrium wage rate and the quantity of labour employed

blocks.alt: Supply and demand graph showing wage on the y-axis and quantity of labour on the x-axis, with intersecting lines labelled SL, DL1, and DL2.
blocks.caption: A rise in the demand for labour increases the price of labour

blocks.md:
- A rise in the demand for websites will cause a rise in the demand for graphic designers** (derived demand)**
- The demand  curve for labour will **shift right from DL**<sub>**1**</sub>** to DL**<sub>**2**</sub>

  - There is **a rise in the equilibrium wage rate to P**<sub>**2**</sub>
  - There is **a rise in the equilibrium quantity **of labour employed** to Q**<sub>**2**</sub>

blocks.name: The Effect of a Fall in Supply of Labour

blocks.text: The Effect of a Fall in the Supply of Labour

blocks.md:
- A fall in the supply of labour will shift the supply curve of labour to the left
- This causes an increase in the equilibrium wage rate and a fall in quantity of labour employed

blocks.alt: Supply and demand graph showing wage rate versus quantity of labour. Lines S, S1 for supply and D for demand intersecting at W, Q and W1, Q1.
blocks.caption: A fall in the supply of graphic designers will cause the wage to rise to W2 and the quantity of graphic designers employed to fall to Q2

blocks.md:
- A fall in the supply of graphic designers as they switch to different jobs will impact the labour in the graphic design industry
- The supply curve of labour will **shift left**

  - There is **a rise in the equilibrium wage rate to W**<sub>**1**</sub>
  - There is **a fall in the equilibrium quantity **of graphic designers employed** from Q to Q**<sub>**1**</sub>
